secs.h2: Common Plumbing Problems We See in Millcreek Homes
blocks: p
Most of the plumbing problems we see in Millcreek homes trace back to aging pipes, mature trees, and hard water. Our 24-hour plumbers routinely handle:
ul
Root-damaged sewer lines: Large shade trees in Canyon Rim and East Millcreek send roots into older clay and cast-iron sewer pipes, causing clogs and backups.
Corroded galvanized pipes: Homes built before 1980 often have aging galvanized pipes that rust from the inside, reducing water pressure.
Frozen pipes: Cold winter days can freeze and burst pipes running through crawl spaces, garages, and exterior walls, especially in foothill homes near Mount Olympus.
Hidden leaks: Pinhole leaks in copper supply lines or under slabs can go unnoticed for months and slowly drive up your water bills.

secs.h2: Why does my water heater run out of hot water so fast?
blocks: p
If your water heater runs out of hot water fast, sediment buildup in the tank is likely the cause. Minerals settle in the tank and take up space meant for hot water.

secs.h2: How do I know if I have a slab leak?
blocks: p

Warm spots on the floor, running water sounds, and a sudden jump in your water bill are the most common signs of a slab leak. If you notice any of these indicators, contact our team as soon as possible for inspection.

secs.h2: How often should I have my plumbing inspected?

We recommend annual plumbing inspections for most homes. Older Millcreek homes near large trees can also benefit from regular camera inspections to spot root intrusion or failing lines early.
